question:
An 68-year-old male patient with stage 5 chronic kidney disease secondary to antineutrophilic
cytoplasmic antigen-positive vasculitis presents for follow-up. His medical history includes mild
cognitive impairment, long-standing hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and ischemic cardiomyopathy.
Current medications include torsemide, metoprolol, amlodipine, atorvastatin, calcium acetate, and
aspirin. He reports mild anorexia but denies nausea, vomiting, or pruritus. On examination, his blood
pressure is 143/54 mm Hg, and his heart rate is 71 beats per minute. Fine basilar rales are noted, with
a normal cardiac examination and no rub. Trace peripheral edema is present, and there is no asterixis.
Recent laboratory results reveal the following: | | Patient value | Reference range | | --- | --- | --- | |
Serum creatinine (mg/dL) | 5.2 | 0.8–1.3 | | Hemoglobin (g/dL) | 11.0 | 13.5–17.5 | | Erythrocyte
sedimentation rate (mm/hr) | 15 | 0–17 | | Calcium (mg/dL) | 9.2 | 9.0–10.5 | | Potassium (mEq/L) | 5.2 |
3.5–5.0 | | Blood urea nitrogen (mg/dL) | 62 | 10–20 | | Bicarbonate (mEq/L) | 23 | 21–30 | | Phosphorus
(mg/dL) | 3.5 | 3.0–4.5 | | Estimated glomerular filtration rate (mL/min/1.73 m²) | 9 | ≥60 | | Albumin
(g/dL) | 4.0 | 3.5–5.5 | Urinalysis shows 1+ protein by dipstick, with microscopy revealing 0–2 red cells
per high-power field and no red-cell casts. His serum creatinine has increased from 4.2 mg/dL eight
weeks ago to 5.2 mg/dL. Which of the following management strategies is most appropriate for this
patient? Answer Choices: (A) Recommend renal transplantation evaluation immediately (B) Administer
calcium carbonate to manage hyperphosphatemia (C) Prescribe sodium polystyrene sulfonate for
hyperkalemia (D) Recommend intermittent hemodialysis (E) Recommend home hemodialysis (F) Start
peritoneal dialysis to improve uremic symptoms (G) Initiate erythropoiesis-stimulating agents
immediately (H) Continue current medical care without dialysis (I) Initiate aggressive fluid removal with
diuretics (J) Initiate treatment with prednisone
 A. Initiate treatment with prednisone
B. Continue current medical care without dialysis
C. Initiate aggressive fluid removal with diuretics
D. Initiate erythropoiesis-stimulating agents immediately
E. Recommend renal transplantation evaluation immediately
F. Recommend intermittent hemodialysis
G. Recommend home hemodialysis
H. Start peritoneal dialysis to improve uremic symptoms
I. Prescribe sodium polystyrene sulfonate for hyperkalemia
J. Administer calcium carbonate to manage hyperphosphatemia
